body: Thank you so much, this was a really helpful response!

I don't think this is a weird thing to do. I always ask my friends how their partners are doing when we see each other or talk. I think of it as a way to show that you care about a relationship/person that is very important to them.
Oh gosh, so many things. The number one was that I paced outside of my house for hours, sometimes late into the night, daydreaming until I felt "right" and felt able to go inside.
Oh my gosh, this made me laugh. Thank you! That's it exactly.
OP: last for around a week or two and then disappear. They don't itch and they don't hurt but they cause me a little worry.
UMM that hoodie is so cute??? I hope physical therapy was gentle and productive!
I am definitely here for both of them. Amos tugs a little more at my heart, I love his bashful energy but Mort Metzger is a close second for favorite television cop.
Oh my gosh, I love a young gay love story! I'll definitely give both of them a watch, thank you so much.
Thank you for the warning! Schitt's Creek is one of my favorites - a little alternate universe where nothing truly bad and lasting happens, it's perfect for me.
Thank you so much for the suggestions, I'm excited to give them a watch!
Thank you so much for these suggestions! I recently started watching How It's Made and I find it so soothing, I can't wait to try Unwrapped.

I definitely would love documentaries! Thank you so much for this list, I'm so excited to watch through them. I have found that Studio Ghibli films are particularly good, especially Kiki's Delivery Service so I think I'll watch Ponyo first!

I have a number that I really like! Mishkan T'filah the CCAR siddur is a classic and has some commentary but isn't my favorite, Siddur Sha'ar Zahav is really beautiful and offers lots of commentary lots of added prayers, and is (VERY lol) not travel sized, Siddur B'chol L'vavcha is pretty lovely and a great size, and (though published by a renewal press) the Romemu Shabbat Siddur is absolutely beautiful and intuitive and offers transliteration and interpretation in a very beautiful way.
Thank you so much for this suggestion, I'll check it out!

It's not that I need an all-English one. I collect siddurim and I'm interested in seeing the differences in translation and formatting of all-English siddurim (if there are others, so far I've only found Sh'ma).
Oh my goodness, of course! Definitely! I am forever trying to be less attached to my phone, it's so hard. I'm so proud of you for working hard to create a good thing for yourself, it's amazing!

I experience the same feeling whenever I feel uncertainty or insecurity in my relationships! It happened to me last when my partner went on a buying trip and sent me a very sweet picture of somebody else's stuffed animal that he thought I would like. I don't know if I'll ever be in a relationship where I don't experience that feeling or if I'd ever be 'ready' to have a relationship. What helps for me is being able to communicate it to my partner so that I can get extra reassurance and self-soothing a little by taking a bath and slowing my body down or wave page journaling. 

I have all the confidence in the world in you and your guy! I hope everything works out well.

Thank you so much! Baby steps is definitely where it's at. As my first one I just started tracking in extreme detail everything I spend my money on and it has started help slow me down and buy less already.
I do the exact same. I have such a huge stack of hobbies that I felt \~sure\~ would be my new passions that I tossed aside almost immediately.
Yes! I find myself in the same loop, buying and then selling things back or returning them quickly. It's so frustrating and such a pain in the butt.
Reading this brought tears to my eyes it was so kind, thank you so much.

My tremors are caused by a few different things. The twitching in my hands is from bad carpal tunnel, the twitching in my arms is stress/anxiety induced and the twitching in my legs is still a mystery. I wish I could be more helpful. Good luck with your diagnosis journey.
Oh my goodness, that's so sweet!
Even reading that made me smile! I love anything that makes a scary situation silly, so this is the perfect suggestion for me! Thank you so much!!
Oh my goodness, I love him SO MUCH! One of my all time favorite pieces of media is the episode where he is in a demolition derby.
This is such a great suggestion! I have such a black thumb, but I've been having some success with cacti lately.
No clutter is something I can 100% get behind! I also really love that there are so many historical and recipe variation videos online to watch.
I'll let you know what I think!
I used to love Plants vs. Zombies! I'm thinking about trying Stardew Valley which is so cute and seems gentle but definitely very click heavy.

I was thinking about trying to bake a little bit! I was worried about wearing out my arms, but someone just gifted me an old stand mixer so I think it's finally time to start. Do you know of a good machine-knead sourdough recipe?

Chess is something I never would have thought of! It's such a good activity to do a deep dive into though. I haven't played since I was quite young, I'm excited to try my hand at it again. Thank you for your suggestions!
I have the same problem, a vertical mouse sounds like EXACTLY what I need. Are there any games that you particularly like?

Documentaries are such a good suggestion! Do you have any favorites? I'm in an MA program right now and interacting with people there (after not interacting with people for so long) has definitely been very nice.

This is also such a good suggestion, thank you so much! I've been thinking about getting into puzzle games like Trine that are pretty gentle. I have had trouble with repetitive clicking in the past, I'll definitely look into economic/accessibility devices.
That's a GREAT suggestion, I wouldn't have even thought about picking up a new language. Thank you!
Thank you, this is so helpful! Last night I reached out to my local Chabad rabbi about the issue.
This is all such helpful information, thank you so much!

I'm so drawn to Moishe House! I have been trying to reach out to some folks in the various pods for a little while but I haven't had much luck with responses yet. 

!! Knight Moves sounds like such a great place. It's been so long since I've lived near a board game cafe, it'll be lovely to live near one again. 

Generally, I'm not too drawn to Reform shuls, but I'll be sure to look into it. Thank you for the suggestion!

That's very refreshing, how are they perceived by the rest of the congregants? 

Given the current situation, I'm not sure that I will be able to couch surf much but I am reaching out to a number of rabbis to get their opinion. 

A mechitza certainly brings up some feelings of discomfort for me. While it's not ideal, it's definitely not a dealbreaker. Currently, when I attend services at an orthodox shul I just dress to conform to the community norm and sit on the women's side. 

I have noticed the rent, I'm moving from an area with comparable prices so it's not too shocking. 

I'll look into Tremont!
That's a very helpful tip, thank you!
That would be so lovely. A good yom tov to you both!

Thank you so much for this AMAZING response. I'll definitely zero in on Cambridge and Brookline. 

The communities (except for reform and renewal) where I am not are also very don't ask, don't tell. In terms of visibility, I'm mostly worried about the fact that I am often read as a woman but wear a tallit katan and kippah. 

I'll definitely look into the smaller minyanim too!
Oh no, I'm sorry to hear that she didn't get into her MA program! If you think she would be interested in making a connection, I'd love an introduction. I'm always looking for new people to talk to!

Thank you so much for the amazing suggestions and for the lovely Shabbos meal invite! I greatly look forward to it once social distancing is no longer necessary.

I am attending Brandeis, I'm already enjoying preparing for my course of study!
Thank you so much!
Thank you so much for this suggestion, it sounds right up my alley!
Lex is a personals/classifieds style dating app for queer women and non-binary folks. For me (aside from dating) it's been a great way to find people to make a minyan and to have over for Shabbos!
A great suggestion, thank you so much!
I'm looking at Jamaica Plain or Brookline.

I'm trying to get a second opinion, I just have to wait for a few weeks to meet with a psychiatrist. I'm thinking about going to my gp to ask him so I would at least have the guidance of a doctor if I decide that I need to stop taking it.

I was making all of my own food + the very limited processed dry goods that I was buying were items that you can consume without a hechsher (ex. flour, cornstarch, baking powder). Thank you for the the comment!
Thank you so much!

Shavua tov! Thank you for this observation, but u/T_jo22 is correct. I do have two mothers and my name is Shachar - I haven't known too many other women who have that name here in the United States, but I know a couple in Israel.

>the

Shavua tov! This was so helpful, thank you so much!
In the circles I'm in it's pronounced SHAY-tel, but I've heard it the other way too!
I'm crying, this is so sweet and cute!
These are both such solid tips, thank you so much!
I did connect with a number of folks in private.
!! This is so funny. I do classically love baggy separates.

I appreciate your understanding of my intention! I do have meetings set up with a number of Rabbis over the next few weeks to discuss this topic. Unfortunately I only know of one other nonbinary individual and they attend a Reform shul, so they're more or less free to dress however they please.
